nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
This is the clear reading. It is permissible for the hamza to come "between-between" (bayna bayna, i.e., softened), so you say أرأيت (with softened hamza), and أريت is permissible with the hamza dropped. From ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: أَرَأَيْتَكَ, the kāf being an added mark of address. The between-between hamza is vowelled, of the same measure (as a full hamza), only lightened; thus said Sībawayh. As for the view of whoever said: it is neither quiescent nor vowelled, that is impossible, because if it is not quiescent it is vowelled, and if it is not vowelled it is quiescent; so on his view it would have to be both quiescent and vowelled. The evidence that it is vowelled is the poet's saying: [al-Basīṭ] 588-
أأن رأت رجلا أعشى أضرّ به ... ريب المنون ودهر مفند خبل
(Is it because she saw a dim-sighted man, harmed by the vicissitudes of fate and a time that weakens and deranges?)
If you said أأن (with full hamzas), the metre would be the same. The between-between hamza is often a subject of error, and it is among the most difficult things in grammar. Among the evidence for what we said is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: سَواءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أَأَنْذَرْتَهُمْ [al-Baqara: 6]: if the between-between hamza were quiescent, two quiescent letters would come together. Likewise in أرأيت, the yāʾ is quiescent and the between-between hamza is vowelled; and whoever makes it quiescent and gives the yāʾ kasra has brought something impermissible, with no justification and no construal in Arabic.
«أرأيت» may be from seeing with the eye, in which case there is no omission in the speech; or from seeing with the heart (knowing), in which case the implied form is: "Have you seen the one who denies the Judgement after the proofs have appeared to him — is he not deserving of the punishment of Allah?"

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: Abū Rajāʾ read يَدَعُ الْيَتِيمَ without doubling, i.e., abandons him [Translator's note: the printed vowelling shows the standard يَدُعُّ].

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: وَلا يَحُضُّ عَلى طَعامِ الْمِسْكِينِ (3): al-Farrāʾ said: i.e., he does not take care over the feeding of the poor, nor command it.

nahhas-irab:4-5.t:
Abū al-ʿĀliya said: it is the one who prostrates and goes like this and like this, or turns to his right and his left.
Abū Jaʿfar said: More fitting than this view, because of the high standing of the one who held it and its soundness in Arabic, is what ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, from al-Ḥusayn [Translator's note: so in the text], from al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad, who said: Abū Muʿāwiya narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif, from Muṣʿab ibn Saʿd, from Saʿd ibn Mālik: A man said to him: الَّذِينَ هُمْ عَنْ صَلاتِهِمْ ساهُونَ (5) — is it the soul's talking (to itself) during prayer? He said: All of us experience that; rather it is the one who neglects it (by letting it pass) its time. And in a narration other than that of Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif, Saʿd said: I asked the Prophet ﷺ about الذين هم عن صلاتهم ساهون, and he said: "Those who delay it beyond its time".

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: I.e., they do not pray out of fear of punishment nor in hope of reward, but so that the Muslims may see them and not shed their blood — and they are the hypocrites.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t:
The scholars have discussed its meaning, as was read before Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm, from al-Farrāʾ: Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ narrated to me, from al-Suddī, from ʿAbd Khayr, from ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: al-māʿūn is zakāt. This is narrated from Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn ʿAbbās with variation. And from Ibn ʿAbbās:
al-māʿūn is what people hand to one another (household utensils). Al-Farrāʾ reported from some of the Arabs that al-māʿūn is water, and recited:
[al-Wāfir] 589- يمجّ صبيره الماعون صبّا ("its white cloud spews out water in a downpour"); ṣabīruhu means its clouds. Abū Jaʿfar said: These views go back to one origin, and it is only the withholding [Translator's note: the text reads «الظن», evidently for «الضنّ», "stinginess"] of a small thing which one ought not to withhold; it is derived from al-maʿn, which is the small thing. And Allah knows best.
